prerequisites: Recommended: Basic knowledge of mathematics, physics and mechanics
Prerequisites for the course Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering: Recommended: Basic knowledge of mathematics and physics
Prerequisites for the course Measurement Technology: Recommended: Technical Mechanics I, Experimental Physics, Fundamentals of Electrical Engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Students can reproduce the acquired knowledge about essential fundamentals of electrical engineering.
They can name the electrical engineering characteristic values and describe the relationship between them.
Furthermore, they are able to read and classify simple circuits.
Students have acquired knowledge about the fundamentals of measurement technology and can present this in a structured way.
They can characterize and interpret measurement signals and reproduce the basics of signal processing.
They know the most important causes of measurement deviations and measurement uncertainties and can determine them.
Furthermore, they have knowledge of various measurement methods and principles.
They can explain the specifics of these methods and principles and apply them to technical problems.

syllabus_topics: Electric fields, magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction
Current, voltage, power, resistance, capacity, inductance, transformer, oscillating circuits
Direct current calculation, transient and stationary processes, complex alternating current calculation
Tasks and basic concepts of measurement technology
Measuring device, measurement method, measurement chain
Measurement signals (classification, characteristic values and representation)
Signal processing and evaluation, measurement deviations and measurement uncertainties
Measurement of physical quantities (electrical quantities, mechanical quantities, thermodynamic quantities and optical quantities)
assessment_rules: Credits are awarded when the module sub-examinations are passed and qualified participation is demonstrated. Participation in the Measurement Technology practical course is required to complete the module. It is recommended to attend the practical course associated with the event parallel to the lecture.
